implemented_capabilities.capability: Code property graph ingestion (Python AST) into FalkorDB
implemented_capabilities.notes: ast.NodeVisitor extracts Class/Function/CallSite/INHERITS etc.; MERGE-based idempotent node/edge upserts; SHA-256 incremental skip. Other languages go to generic/fallback regex-style parsers (thin).

implemented_capabilities.capability: Graph algorithm engine (BFS blast radius, Tarjan SCC, PageRank, label-propagation, betweenness, ablation)
implemented_capabilities.notes: Bounded in-memory algorithms over an adjacency pulled from FalkorDB (no GDS/APOC); depth/path caps; shortest_path first tries Cypher shortestPath then BFS fallback. Returns AlgorithmExecutionResult with rationale/explanation.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Persistent agent memory with staleness invalidation via snippet hash
implemented_capabilities.notes: Findings are stored as (:Finding)-[:EVIDENCED_BY]->(:SourceEvidence {file,start/end line,snippet_hash}) with source_revision (git HEAD or file-stat hash). invalidate_stale_findings recomputes SHA-256 of the cited lines and sets is_stale/stale_reason when file deleted, lines changed, or revision advanced. query_semantic_memory excludes stale/quarantined by default.

Checks every file:line citation against disk and every claimed graph path edge against FalkorDB; reports fabricated citations/paths, extracted vs inferred claims, and multi-dimension verification flags (source, graph, scenario, execution receipt, memory persistence, multi-agent handoff).
Deterministic rule-based tool selection keyed on graph topology (fan-in, circuit breaker edge); records decision steps; no LLM needed. The 'causal dependency' demo is a rule table, not learned.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Multi-agent coordination with task leases and handoff edges
implemented_capabilities.notes: Atomic Cypher MATCH...WHERE status='PENDING' OR lease_expires<=now SET claimed_by lease; HANDOFF_TO edges persisted. Four 'roles' are in-process Python methods, not independent agents. Errors are swallowed at debug level.
Ranks tests by graph distance, requires authorize flag before running pytest via subprocess with a 30s timeout.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Benchmark-specific scenario simulators and canned question handlers
implemented_capabilities.notes: Hand-coded state machines for the DeployWeave/OrbitOps/SignalForge/RelayMesh/NexusPay fixture repos shipped under backend/data/repos, keyed on question text (Q51..Q85). This is benchmark-fitted logic, not general-purpose.
_load_default_organizational_catalog() returns a hard-coded in-memory catalog of teams/people/ADRs (ADR-004, ADR-007) for the demo repos; hard-coded demo data, not ingested from any real source.

graph_models_and_cypher: FalkorDB graph per repo: workspace_<repo_id>. Labels (schema.py NodeType): Repository, Revision, File, Module, Class, Function, Method, CallSite, Branch, Queue, StateStore, ExternalService, Test, Config*; memory: Investigation, InvestigationSession, Finding, SourceEvidence, Hypothesis, Procedure, Decision, Observation, AgentTask, Agent; company: Person, Team, DecisionRecord. Edges (RelType): CALLS, IMPORTS, DEFINES, INHERITS, TESTS, DEPENDS_ON, READS_STATE/WRITES_STATE, ENQUEUES/DEQUEUES, RECORDED, REFERENCES, EVIDENCED_BY, PROPOSED, TARGETS, HANDOFF_TO, plus declared-but-unused INVALIDATES and SUPERSEDES (schema.py:100-101; no code writes them - staleness is a property flag). Edge props: provenance, confidence, is_inferred. Cypher is FalkorDB-compatible (shortestPath, variable-length paths); no APOC/GDS. Parameterized $params throughout; f-string interpolation only of clamped integer depths and rel-type lists (tools.py:41-83, algorithms.py:92-99).
algorithms: BFS reachable_nodes/reverse_dependencies with depth_map and max_depth cap (graph/algorithms.py:190-249)
Tarjan SCC for circular dependencies (algorithms.py:292-353, recursive, no recursion guard)
Degree/betweenness centrality, PageRank, label-propagation community detection (algorithms.py:358-528)
Bounded DFS all-paths with max_paths cap (algorithms.py:152-185)
SHA-256 snippet-hash drift detection for stale findings (memory/manager.py:92-106, 693-752)
Atomic Cypher task lease with expiry (agent/multi_agent.py:156-208)
backend_interfaces: FastAPI: GET /health, GET/POST repositories (import local/github/zip), POST /repositories/{id}/index, DELETE repo, POST ingest, GET graph/{repo_id}, POST investigate, POST impact (git diff), GET memory/sessions|findings|hypotheses, POST memory/invalidate (main.py:44-406)
frontend_interfaces: React 18 + Cytoscape: App.tsx (909 lines), components/GraphExplorer.tsx, ImportRepositoryModal.tsx, RepositorySelector.tsx
agent_or_memory_mechanisms: Episodic (InvestigationSession), semantic (Finding+SourceEvidence with snippet_hash and revision), hypothesis lifecycle (unresolved/validated/rejected), procedural memory (Procedure.success_count), staleness invalidation and quarantine of contaminated memories; multi-role handoff with leases. LLM (Gemini) used only in agent/investigator.py; falls back to mock_mode when no key.

Tests run against MockFalkorClient (ENVIRONMENT=test) - the mock pattern-matches Cypher substrings, so tests do not validate real Cypher. README claims 104 passing; not executed by auditor.

backend/app/agent/actions.py:157 - subprocess.run([sys.executable,-m,pytest,test_file,-k,test_name]) executes tests from an imported repo; guarded by authorize flag and 30s timeout, but test_file/test_name derive from parsed repo content (code execution of untrusted repos).
backend/app/agent/test_impact.py:341 - same pytest subprocess execution of target repo tests.

backend/app/repositories/manager.py:245 - git clone of user URL via subprocess (list args, regex-validated github.com URL, 45s timeout); branch arg passed unvalidated to --branch (option-injection risk if value starts with '-').
backend/app/repositories/manager.py:117-127 - import_local allows arbitrary local directory import; forbidden-root check is POSIX-only and bypassable (startswith home exemption).
backend/app/repositories/manager.py:171-187 - ZIP import has zip-slip, size and file-count checks (good) but z.extractall after validation.
backend/app/graph/algorithms.py:92-99 - f-string Cypher interpolates allowed_rel_types and max_depth directly; safe only if callers never pass user-controlled rel types.
backend/app/graph/client.py:87-89,110-112 - property keys interpolated into Cypher as backtick-quoted names (k from node.properties); injection if keys are attacker-controlled.
backend/app/graph/client.py:176-178 - get_all_elements interpolates limit into Cypher f-string.
backend/app/agent/impact.py:198-209 and backend/app/memory/manager.py:58-72 - git subprocess calls with fixed arg lists (low risk).

duplicates_or_overlaps: Overlaps blast-radius traversal (reverse_dependencies), dependency-cycle detection (SCC), RCA-from-diff, test impact selection, and agent memory/provenance. Many sibling hackathon repos in this corpus implement code-graph blast radius; the memory staleness piece is the differentiator.
evidence_drift_relevance: HIGH - GraphMemoryManager stores claims with SourceEvidence(file,line range,snippet_hash,source_revision), detects drift by re-hashing cited lines, marks findings stale with a reason, quarantines contaminated memory, and EvidenceVerifier rejects fabricated citations; however SUPERSEDES/INVALIDATES edges are declared but unused and invalidation does not cascade to dependent decisions.

strongest_reusable_unit.why: Concrete content-hash based evidence drift detection with revision tracking and stale reasons, expressed in parameterized FalkorDB-compatible Cypher; directly maps to Evidence Drift Cascade (claim -> evidence -> hash -> stale flag). Needs a cascade step (traverse EVIDENCED_BY/REFERENCES/DECIDED to invalidate dependents).
strongest_reusable_unit.external_runtime_needed: FalkorDB (via module-level falkor_client singleton; MockFalkorClient fallback); git CLI optional; no LLM key needed

strategy_rationale: Extract the snippet-hash staleness logic, EvidenceVerifier and GraphAlgorithmEngine as a shared engine behind an injected graph client rather than the module-level singleton; do not import the benchmark-fitted scenario/DeployWeave handlers. License is missing so reuse depends on the attested owner permission.
